**Refined prompt:** Diagnose and fix the HTTP 500 returned by the favorite endpoint on this NestJS/TypeORM RealWorld API, working from the repo's recorded conventions and prior bug lessons, citing the exact lines responsible — and change only what causes the 500, flagging adjacent defects rather than folding them in.

## Root cause — confirmed

`UserEntity.favorites` is a plain `@ManyToMany` with no `eager: true` (`src/user/user.entity.ts:33-35`). `ArticleService.favorite()` loads the user without requesting that relation:

```
src/article/article.service.ts:133    const user = await this.userRepository.findOne(id);
src/article/article.service.ts:135    const isNewFavorite = user.favorites.findIndex(...) < 0;
```

So `user.favorites` is `undefined`, not `[]` → `TypeError: Cannot read property 'findIndex' of undefined` → 500 on every `POST /api/articles/:slug/favorite`. This is exactly the case recorded in `LESSONS.md:68-76`, and `.claude/knowledge/schema.md:23` states the same: *"A `userRepository.findOne(id)` returns `favorites === undefined`; you must pass `{ relations: ['favorites'] }`."*

`unFavorite()` has the identical line (`article.service.ts:149`), so `DELETE .../favorite` crashes the same way — same defect, same path, so I included it.

## The patch

The sibling call at `article.service.ts:181` already uses the options-object form, so this mirrors it (TypeORM 0.2.24, per `package.json:46`):

```diff
--- a/src/article/article.service.ts
+++ b/src/article/article.service.ts
@@ -131,7 +131,7 @@
   async favorite(id: number, slug: string): Promise<ArticleRO> {
     let article = await this.articleRepository.findOne({slug});
-    const user = await this.userRepository.findOne(id);
+    const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { id }, relations: ['favorites'] });
 
     const isNewFavorite = user.favorites.findIndex(_article => _article.id === article.id) < 0;
@@ -147,7 +147,7 @@
   async unFavorite(id: number, slug: string): Promise<ArticleRO> {
     let article = await this.articleRepository.findOne({slug});
-    const user = await this.userRepository.findOne(id);
+    const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { id }, relations: ['favorites'] });
 
     const deleteIndex = user.favorites.findIndex(_article => _article.id === article.id);
```

I re-read the file afterwards to be sure nothing was half-written — all 205 lines are intact, lines 133 and 149 still read `findOne(id)`. **Nothing was modified and nothing was verified at runtime; I did not run the app or any test.**

Apply the diff yourself, or grant write access and I'll apply and re-check it.

## Adjacent defects I deliberately did not touch

- **Unknown slug is also a 500 on the same endpoint.** `article.service.ts:132` returns `undefined` for a missing slug, then `article.id` at line 135 throws. Different cause from the one you reported; the spec wants 404. Say the word and I'll add it.
- **`GET /articles?favorited=` has the same undefined-relation crash** at `article.service.ts:45`, *and* line 46 filters `article.authorId IN (:ids)` against article ids — two separate bugs, both already in `LESSONS.md:86-93`.
- **No ownership check** on favorite or anywhere else; `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12` has that as in-flight design work.

One caveat on what I read: I confirmed the route is auth-guarded at `article.module.ts:30`, but I did not open `auth.middleware.ts` or `user.decorator.ts`, so I'm asserting nothing about how `userId` is populated beyond that registration.
